1.explanation:
• options.md – describes the printWidth and proseWrap settings that govern how Prettier wraps and formats Markdown (including tables).  
• configuration.md – explains how to configure Prettier project-wide or via CLI, so you can reproduce the issue with your custom settings.  
• language-support.md – spells out Prettier’s Markdown support, including tables and HTML nodes, giving context to why the all-contributors table is parsed as HTML within Markdown.  
• option-philosophy.md – provides insight into Prettier’s design choices around formatting decisions, useful for understanding why table normalization works the way it does.  
• technical-details.md – dives into the Markdown plugin’s implementation details (including table normalization logic), which you’ll need to modify to detect long separator rows and implement the fallback behavior.
1.bug_scenario: When Prettier formats a Markdown table that contains very long HTML‐only cells (for example, an all-contributors table with `` tags and links), its table normalizing routine calculates the maximum cell width and expands the separator row (the `| :----: |` line) to match that width. In the screenshot, you can see the editor’s status bar reporting a line length of 865 characters and the table’s dividing row full of hundreds of dashes. This is undesirable: we’d rather detect excessively long normalized rows and fall back to the simple three-dash (`:---:`) separators instead of expanding them to match content width.
